models.model: Then the king ordered the harp to be given to Apollonius. Then stillness and silence came about inside the hall. Apollonius took his harp-pick and began to move the harp strings with skill, and mingled the harp's sound with a pleasant song. The king himself and everyone who was present cried out in a loud voice and praised him. After this Apollonius put aside the harp and performed, presenting many fine things there—something unfamiliar and unusual to the people. Every one of the things he performed pleased them all greatly.

models.model: Ondrǣdendum is dative plural because the people are beneficiaries. Hine is accusative because it is the object governed by fear within that phrase. The outer case and the inner verb's government remain separate.

The participle names people characterized by fearing or hunger and takes the case demanded by the noun phrase's role. It is nonfinite: present participle is not a person/tense statement, and these phrases have no finite verb.
